transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today? Is there something specific that's been troubling you?.

I guess what brought me in is… some evenings after work I end up eating a lot more than I planned. Especially if I’ve been really strict with myself during the day. I’ll have dinner, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, leftovers, sweets—just a lot of food within a couple hours. It’s been bothering me.
When you eat a lot after work, do you feel like you can’t control how much you eat or stop yourself once you start?

Yes. Once I get started on those nights, I feel like I keep going back to the kitchen even though I’m telling myself to stop. I don’t really feel like I’m back in control until I’m already uncomfortably full.
Do you often feel uncomfortably full after these episodes, even to the point of being physically uncomfortable?
Yes, I do. On those nights, once I start, I keep going back even while I’m telling myself to stop. I usually don’t feel like I’m back in control until I’m already uncomfortably full.
After these episodes where you eat a lot and feel uncomfortably full, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I don’t usually make myself throw up or anything like that. But the next day I’ll try to “make up for it” by skipping breakfast and lunch, or I’ll take a really long hike, or push myself harder at softball conditioning even if I’m already tired.

Do you ever try to get rid of the food or calories after these episodes by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing a lot more exercise than usual? Just so I understand, even if you don’t do it every time, have you done it at all?

Yeah… not vomiting or laxatives, no. But I have done the other kind of thing. The next day I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, telling myself I’m making up for what I ate. Or I’ll go on a really long hike, or push myself harder at softball conditioning even when I’m already tired.
Can you recall if these episodes of eating a lot happen within a specific window of time, like over the course of a couple of hours, rather than being spread out through the whole evening?

Yes, it’s usually within a couple of hours. Like after work, especially if I’ve been really strict with myself all day, I’ll start with dinner and then keep going—cereal, crackers, leftovers, something sweet. It’s not like it’s spread out all night so much as it all happens pretty quickly.
How often do these episodes happen? Would you say they occur at least once a week on average?

Yes, I’d say at least once a week. For the past few months it’s been most weeks—usually one or two nights where I eat way more than I meant to. Then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time (within a couple of hours), loss of control during the episodes, and subsequent compensatory behaviors such as fasting and excessive exercise. These behaviors occur at least once a week on average. This presentation aligns with binge eating disorder (F50.2). Bulimia nervosa (F50.0) is ruled out as the patient does not engage in self-induced vomiting or laxative misuse.
